svg.title: Poisson exceedance probability — EQ-Live Türkiye
svg.desc: Figure. Probability of at least one earthquake with magnitude ≥ M within t = 10, 25, 50 and 100 years under a time-independent Poisson model, P(≥M; t) = 1 − exp[−λ(≥M)·t], for the whole of each region: (a) Türkiye [Tarihsel Katalog (ISC+EMSC, statik); 1998-01-01 – 2026-09-14; A = 1,094,914 km²; GK74 off]; (b) Marmara [Tarihsel Katalog (ISC+EMSC, statik); 1998-01-01 – 2026-09-14; A = 70,249 km²; GK74 on]; (c) Doğu Anadolu [Tarihsel Katalog (ISC+EMSC, statik); 1998-01-01 – 2026-09-14; A = 122,195 km²; GK74 off]. λ(≥M) = (N(≥Mc)/T)·10^[−b(M − Mc)]; b is the Bender (1983) maximum-likelihood estimate for magnitude-grouped data (reference Aki–Utsu values in the table) and Mc a single completeness magnitude. Shaded bands: 95% intervals from a joint parametric bootstrap of a and b (B = 2000, seed 20261027). Dashed lines: extrapolation beyond the largest observed magnitude. Solid vertical line: magnitude at which the mean recurrence interval Tr = 1/λ(≥M) equals the catalogue duration T (M = Mc + log₁₀N/b); to its right the G–R relation is extended beyond the observation period. Grey area: Tr > 10T, high extrapolation uncertainty. The 10T bound is not a universally accepted scientific threshold but an operational criterion for classifying the uncertainty of extrapolation beyond the observation period. The model assumes a constant rate and independent events (GK74 declustering does not guarantee independence); it is not an earthquake forecast. Source: EQ-Live Türkiye.
